subject: using the column with number of individuals to produce reports

messages.author: af2b16d60afe57cd
messages.subject: using the column with number of individuals to produce reports
parts:
Dear group,

I am using the reports produced from "surveyReport" (CamtrapR, from an excel file with species, not from photos) to estimate the RAI´s (Relative abundance or capture freq) per species.  For this, I used "report_test[[5]]" which provides the number of events (n_events) per species needed. However, when doing the calculations I noticed that the number of events from the reports is the number of rows the species appears in the dataset, not the real number of individuals which we include in a separate column. Therefore using the rows will bias the results. So, I am wondering if there is a way to include this column of #of individuals to produce the reports. That would be one solution and would be great because anything containing the number of events could be used directly from the reports without bias. 

Another solution that occurs to me would be to create new rows based on the values of the cell containing the number of individuals and repeat them as many times as needed (see below). Not sure if this is the best solution, though, since we have species that are found in groups of 10-40 individuals, so maybe not practical.

I would appreciate any feedback on this matter. 

Thank you very much in advance.
Stay safe!
Lain

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: using the column with number of individuals to produce reports
parts:
Hi Lain, 
I think the simplest solution would be to create the desired output yourself directly from the record table. Something like this:

data("recordTableSample")

# add fake n_individual column for demonstration
recordTableSample$n_individual <- rpois(nrow(recordTableSample), 1) + 1

# sum up n_individual by station and species
out <- aggregate(recordTableSample$n_individual,
                 by = list(recordTableSample$Station, 
                           recordTableSample$Species),
                 FUN = sum,
                 drop = TRUE)   # set to FALSE if needed (to match format of reportTest[[5]], but then also replace NA with 0)

# tidy up output
out <- out[order(out$Group.1, out$Group.2), ]
colnames(out) <- c("Station", "Species", "sum_individuals")
rownames(out) <- NULL

> head(out)
   Station Species sum_individuals
1 StationA     PBE               8
2 StationA     VTA               7
3 StationB     MNE               4
4 StationB     PBE              17
5 StationB     VTA               5
6 StationC     EGY              16

That would be the sum of individuals for each station and species. Is that what you were looking for?

You wrote:

That would be one solution and would be great because anything containing the number of events could be used directly from the reports without bias.

I am a little confused here, because the current output (report_test[[5]]) gives the number of events already. Did you mean number of individuals?

Also, keep in mind that the same individuals may be recorded in different images. So simply summing up the number of individuals from all images of a species at a station will give misleading results and hugely overestimate true numbers of individuals.

Best regards and stay safe too,
Jürgen

messages.author: af2b16d60afe57cd
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: using the column with number of individuals to produce reports
parts:
Dear Juergen,

Thank you very much for your quick response!
Yes, that´s what I was looking for. I need the format of report 5, since I need to create a  matrix of species per site. Many thanks! 

That´s a valid concern that you raised. Most of the time the independent records (or events) have one single animal in the picture so not an issue. In rare occasions, we can have two animals in the same photo and very few other events (e.g. felids), not adding the individuals in that single photo could also underestimate the abundances, don´t you think?. But yes, it could also show more individuals than there actually are, especially for those social species that forage in groups for long time (antelopes in our case). We will have to set a criterium to balance this tradeoff depending on our questions and species involved in the analysis. The criteria of independence would help too. Maybe increasing the time frame for those very common or social species is better (more than 60 minutes or so), don´t you think? It is a bit of a tradeoff that we need to define after exploring our data set. Now, having being able to do it automatically will help us a lot.  I am curious though, would you recommend just ignore the number of individuals in the pictures as a "rule of thumb"? Thanks for your comment. 

Best wishes,
Lain
